solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Baseball players each finding home in London?

parts.note: batters are the players who take turns to hit in baseball
EA is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price tags

explanation.surface: Where do baseball players each find a place to live in London?
explanation.walkthrough: Battersea Dogs Home is a famous London animal shelter, which is the 'home' meant; the question mark flags that it is a home for strays rather than people.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is the London district famous for its dogs' rescue shelter, so it names a home there.

clue.text: Graduate set up equipment for printing process

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: set up in a down entry means written upwards, so the word for equipment reads in reverse

parts.note: kit is equipment

explanation.surface: A graduate sets up the equipment for a printing job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns KIT into TIK in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Batik is a method of dyeing and patterning cloth using wax resist, a textile printing technique.

clue.text: React with irritation, greatly reducing one's shock?

definitions.meaning: to react with great frustration or exasperation
a shock is a thick mass of hair, which pulling out would thin

explanation.surface: Getting angry and thinning out a fright one has had.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' looks like a fright, but is a shock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes acting with extreme frustration, pulling at one's own hair in despair.

clue.text: Stress politician in east suffers on island

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside another

parts.note: to have an illness is to suffer it
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician posted to the east suffers stress on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffers' is HAS in the sense of having an illness; 'in' sets the politician between the E and that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is weight or importance placed on something, which is stress.

clue.text: Ancient Jew unhappy leader in Rome close to gate

parts.note: sad means unhappy
Duce, Italian for leader, was Mussolini's title

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An ancient Jew stands unhappily near the gate as the Roman leader approaches.
explanation.walkthrough: Il Duce, 'the leader', was the title Mussolini took in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sadducees were a Jewish sect of the Second Temple period, opposed to the Pharisees.

clue.text: Settle bill, like Wallace's four men?

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a bill posted up
Edgar Wallace wrote the thriller The Four Just Men

explanation.surface: Paying a bill, as Edgar Wallace's four men might?
explanation.walkthrough: Edgar Wallace was a British thriller writer whose novel The Four Just Men supplies JUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust a claim or account is to settle it; to adjust is also to set right.

clue.text: Pernickety female quietly leaving Bombay, perhaps

indicators.note: something leaving a word is dropped out of it, so these letters go

parts.note: the Bombay is a breed of black cat, so an example of a pussy
P is piano, the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A fussy woman slipping silently away from the Indian city of Bombay.
explanation.walkthrough: Bombay reads as the old name of Mumbai, but here it is the cat breed; 'leaving' takes the P off PUSSY to give USSY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pernickety is fastidious about small details, the core sense of being hard to please.

clue.text: Blonde with casual attitude swallowed up by bog

indicators.note: swallowed up by places these letters inside the word for the bog

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, a bog
lax means slack or careless

explanation.surface: A carefree blonde walker is swallowed up by a bog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with casual attitude' is one phrase for the slack word; 'swallowed up by' has the marsh word enclose it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flaxen hair is pale yellow like flax fibre, so it describes a blonde.

clue.text: Speak bluntly, seeing film supplied by trendies?

parts.note: to film a scene is to shoot it
something supplied by a source comes from it
the hip are fashionable people, trendies

explanation.surface: Speaking frankly about a movie made with fashionable people's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoot from the hip is to speak or act impulsively and directly, like a gunfighter drawing without aiming.

clue.text: Cry of joy about desert transformed very recently

indicators.note: about means around, so the cry wraps the other letters

parts.note: yay is a cry of delight

indicators.note: transformed means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A joyful shout over a desert made to bloom only lately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges the desert's letters into ESTERD; 'about' wraps the cry of joy round them.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning on the previous day, used loosely for a very short time ago.

clue.text: Deceived, having leave withdrawn, broken by pressure

indicators.note: a word broken by another letter has that letter forced into its middle
withdrawn is read as drawn back, so the word for leaving is written in reverse

parts.note: to leave is to depart
P is the scientific symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Someone deceived out of their holiday leave, cancelled under pressure from the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'withdrawn' turns DEPART into TRAPED, and 'broken by' splits it to take P, giving TRAP-P-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be trapped is to be caught out by a trick, so tricked or deceived.

clue.text: Resentful judge has militant executed

indicators.note: an executed person is beheaded, so the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a militant campaigner is zealous

explanation.surface: A judge orders a militant activist put to death.
explanation.walkthrough: 'executed' means beheaded here: ZEALOUS loses its head, Z, to leave EALOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jealousy is resentment at another's advantages, so the two adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: Social misfit returned, having lost a Swedish coin

indicators.note: having lost something means one letter is dropped from what remains
returned is read as sent back, so the word for the misfit runs backwards

parts.note: an anorak is British slang for an obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast, named after the coat trainspotters wear

explanation.surface: An outcast comes home having lost a Swedish coin on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns ANORAK into KARONA, and 'having lost a' drops its first A to leave KRONA.
explanation.definitionFit: The krona is Sweden's currency unit, so a Swedish coin.

clue.text: Uncover articles on a French novel

indicators.note: placed on, meaning written after, in an across entry

parts.note: un is the French for a
She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard
a and the are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: A reviewer uncovering the articles written about some French novel.
explanation.walkthrough: She, H. Rider Haggard's adventure novel, is a crossword favourite; 'on' sets the two articles after the novel in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsheathe a sword is to draw it from its scabbard, uncovering the blade.

clue.text: Fish this person's caught in parts of Wales

indicators.note: something caught in a container sits inside it
parts of is read as the place name broken into pieces and reassembled

parts.note: this person's is read as I've, short for I have

explanation.surface: Fish that this angler has landed in various corners of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts of' breaks the country's name into ALEWS; 'caught in' holds the contraction for 'this person has' inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Alewives are North Atlantic herring-like fish that run up rivers to spawn.

clue.text: Part of speech club employee finally made, being in voice

indicators.note: being in places these letters inside the word for the voice

parts.note: active is one of the two grammatical voices of a verb
a DJ, disc jockey, is employed to play music in a club

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before

explanation.surface: A club DJ's speech, finally made, is delivered in good voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'voice' is the grammatical term (active or passive), not singing; 'being in' places the disc jockey and E after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective is one of the word classes, or parts of speech, describing a noun.

clue.text: Little resistance disturbs this form of jazz

indicators.note: something that disturbs a word gets in among its letters

parts.note: a tad is a little bit
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A jazz fan barely minds a bit of resistance to this style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little resistance' looks like one phrase but splits into TAD and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Trad is short for traditional jazz, the New Orleans revival style popular in Britain in the 1950s.

clue.text: Hanger-on, one locking up pound by farm building

parts.note: a barn is a farm building

indicators.note: locking up has the outer word enclose the other letter

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
L, from Latin libra, stands for a pound

explanation.surface: A clingy type, one who locks up a stray pound near the barn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is the ace of cards, and 'pound' is the L of the old £sd money; 'locking up' has the card enclose it.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnacle clings to rocks and hulls, so figuratively it is a persistent follower or hanger-on.

clue.text: Greedy chap with plenty of room, ignoring the odds

parts.note: Ed is a man's name, so a chap

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out of the word

parts.note: spacious means having plenty of room
SP is the starting price, the betting odds on a horse at the off

explanation.surface: A greedy fellow with a big house who doesn't care about the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, starting price, is the bookmakers' odds when a race begins; 'ignoring' drops it from SPACIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Edacious is a literary word for voracious or gluttonous, so greedy.

clue.text: Demon driver in Paris I hated unreservedly at first

parts.note: je is French for I

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letters of the two words just before it

explanation.surface: A Paris motorist confesses to hating reckless drivers outright.
explanation.walkthrough: Jehu is the Old Testament king who 'driveth furiously', hence a joking name for a fast or reckless driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Jehu is a facetious name for a fast, furious driver, from the biblical king's chariot driving.

clue.text: Haphazardly hosted party, then left in motor yacht

parts.note: to run an event is to host it
a do is a party

indicators.note: in places one letter inside another

parts.note: MY is the prefix used for a motor yacht's name

explanation.surface: A careless host throws a party, then sets off in his motor yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: MY is the abbreviation for motor yacht, as HMS is for a naval ship; 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something randomly means without plan or order, which is haphazard.

clue.text: Courage of woman round ancient city

parts.note: Val is a woman's name
O is round in shape
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A woman's courage as she circles an ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' is a shape, the letter O, not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Valour is great bravery, especially in battle, a synonym for courage.

clue.text: Secret deliveries taken into court

indicators.note: taken into places these letters inside the abbreviation

parts.note: an over in cricket is a set of six deliveries, or balls bowled

explanation.surface: Secret parcels are carried into the courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled by one bowler, so 'deliveries' gives OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert means concealed or clandestine, done in secret.

clue.text: Outstanding feature, a draw at new part of city

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face that sticks out
to draw a load is to tow it

explanation.surface: A striking attraction, a draw for visitors at a new district of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' reads as excellent but means literally standing out, as a chin does from the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinatown is a district of a city where many Chinese people live and trade.

clue.text: Salmon served in hotel in my quarter

indicators.note: served in has the letter sitting inside the exclamation like food on a plate

parts.note: coo and my are both exclamations of surprise
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: Salmon is served in the hotel restaurant in my part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, as in 'my goodness', which COO also is; 'served in' places H inside COO.
explanation.definitionFit: The cohoe, or coho, is a Pacific salmon species also called silver salmon.

clue.text: Composition — first of Elgar's symphonies, for example

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of each of the two words that follow

parts.note: say introduces an example, like for example

explanation.surface: A piece of writing on the first of Elgar's symphonies, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of' applies to both Elgar's and symphonies, giving E and S.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is a short written composition, as set for school pupils.

clue.text: Element the same, only different one old poet's misrepresented

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown wrongly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old poet is misquoted: one element is the same, just different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' rearranges O and the poet's letters into SOTOPE; the definition is a cheeky description rather than a dictionary term.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotopes are forms of one chemical element with the same protons but different numbers of neutrons.

clue.text: Reluctant to wear church's habiliments?

indicators.note: one item wearing another has it around it, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, so its possessive gives CES
loth means reluctant or unwilling

explanation.surface: Unwilling to put on the vestments the church requires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to wear' is reversed in effect: the church's letters wear LOTH, wrapping round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Habiliments is an old or formal word for garments or dress.

clue.text: Record books kept by English queen

indicators.note: kept by places these letters inside the ones that follow

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher for the queen
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An English queen keeps records in her books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'books' are the New Testament ones, a common crossword usage; 'kept by' has them held inside English and queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data in a ledger or log is to record it.

clue.text: A man's work introducing extremely holy religious doctrine

parts.note: Theo is a man's name, so his possessive gives THEOS
op is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: introducing the extremes of the next word brings in just its outermost letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A man's writings introduce a profoundly holy doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A man's' is any man's name in the possessive; here Theo's. 'introducing extremely' brings in only the outside letters of holy.
explanation.definitionFit: Theosophy is a mystical religious philosophy claiming insight into the divine nature.
